messages.author: 40f924322dfa37ae
messages.subject: Question using micro_era5
parts:
Hi Mike,

I am trying to get the microclimate of a location using micro_era5. However, it always returns an error. I don't know what's wrong with it. Is there any possible solution to this? 

Here is the code for micro_era5():

lon=120.98
lat=38.95
year=2018
dstart="01/09/2018"
dfinish="30/09/2018"

lon_min<-floor(lon/5)*5 #the starting longitude of corresponding section
                        #(we divided the earth by every 5 degrees in longitude)
spatial=paste0("/home/2/era5_singlelevel/",year,"/",lon_min,"_",lon_min+5)

#run microclimate model
micro<-try(micro_era5(#Type in parameters that are not default
                      spatial = spatial,
                      loc = c(lon,lat),
                      dstart = dstart,
                      dfinish = dfinish))

And the error results are as follows:

If program is crashing, try run.gads = 2. downloading DEM via package elevatr Accessing raster elevation [=========================] 100% Mosaicing & Projecting Note: Elevation units are in meters. extracting weather data locally from /home/2/era5_singlelevel/2018/120_125 Distance weighting applied. Diurnal temperature range correction applied. Distance weighting applied. computing radiation and elevation effects with package microclima Downscaling radiation and wind speed Calculating meso-scale terrain effects Accessing raster elevation [=========================] 100% Mosaicing & Projecting Note: Elevation units are in meters. Error in .rawTransform(projfrom, projto, xy) : no slot of name "ptr" for this object of class "SpatVector" In addition: Warning messages: 1: PROJ support is provided by the sf and terra packages among others 2: PROJ support is provided by the sf and terra packages among others 3: In microclima::microclimaforNMR(lat = longlat[2], long = longlat[1], : Data sequence in UTC/GMT. Some or all dates using system timezone are in CST 4: PROJ support is provided by the sf and terra packages among others 5: PROJ support is provided by the sf and terra packages among others

Your help would be most appreciated!

Best,
Bingbing Liu

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Question using micro_era5
parts:
Hi Bingbing Liu,
Have you installed the latest version of the package? It might be due to the rgdal issues which should now be removed if you have the latest versions of both NicheMapR and microclima.
All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Private message regarding: Question using micro_era5
parts:
Hi Bingbing Liu,

They are all just warnings and none are of concern re the calculations. 

This one: Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified
is nothing to do with NicheMapR and a quick google suggests it's due to you running as root
This one: The following objects are masked from ‘package:mcera5’: clearskyrad, julday, siflat, solalt, solartime, windheight
is due to two packages having the same names for objects and this one: Registered S3 method overwritten by 'httr': method from print.cache_info hoardr
is I think because of packages having common function names
This one: Warning messages: 1: In fun(libname, pkgname) : couldn't connect to display ":0"
is something specific to your system
This one: PROJ support is provided by the sf and terra packages among others
looks like there's something still lingering from the retirement of rgdal but it won't be causing you issues
and this one: In microclima::microclimaforNMR(lat = longlat[2], long = longlat[1], : Data sequence in UTC/GMT. Some or all dates using system timezone are in CST
is just to warn you to be careful about which time zone you've got for your dates when you're comparing things.

Note however that I found an issue with micro_ncep and micro_era5 to do with time zones that will sometimes result in an error because the rainhr vector isn't constructed properly. It's fixed now in the latest version on github and I'll update the release shortly.

All the best,
Mike
